column1: # Labs under scripts/*-in-docker.sh that a workflow cannot run, and why.
# Read by scripts/ci/check-lab-coverage.py; a row is a dated claim, not an exemption.
# A lab whose verdict CI could produce has no row here: it is named on an executable
# line of a workflow instead. See the gate's docstring for the two rules.

column7: install.sh downloads the published release artifact from GitHub and installs that, so a green here describes what the release endpoint serves rather than the commit under test; CI has no released artifact of its own to install, and pointing the lab at a workflow-built tarball would stop testing the installer's URL, key and digest handling

npm install resolves the platform packages the root package.json pins, and two of them (chaos-code-win32-x64 and chaos-code-win32-arm64 at 0.2.110) are published only as security placeholders, so the lab is red on the registry's state rather than on this commit; publishing those packages is a release action, which this repository does not perform from CI

the rust, clippy and script-job steps run the same command list natively on every push, so a container leg in CI would measure the image build and the cargo volume caches instead of the change; the full sweep inside the image runs to about two hours and would hold every merge behind a rebuild of the verification image
